old: Open your eyes. Move. Touch something textured. Name five objects. End the deeper practice for the day.
new: This is the time for you to open your eyes, to start moving again, to start touching the textured world again. Name the five things you can see. Your practice for today is over.

old: Return to food, sleep, chores, humility, and somebody who will disagree with you.
new: Eat, sleep, work your chores, be humble again

old: “If this insight is real, it will survive sleep, food, time, humility, and feedback.”
new: Mantra: “Will this insight survive sleeping and eating and time, humility and feedback?

old: Ask the bliss to become specific.
new: Have it ask you to be specific about the bliss

old: “What task, boundary, meal, rest, repair, or conversation does love require next?”
new: “What can you do to be loving right now?”

old: Don’t pry.
new: Do n't pry

old: “Show me the capacity before the content.”
new: “Ask it to show you the next capacity instead of the next content.”

old: Sit up and open your eyes.
new: Sit up and open your eyes

old: “What real action is this fantasy replacing?”
new: “What real action is this fantasy replacing?”

old: A presupposition hides an assumption inside a sentence. Use that power only to presume choice, timing, capacity, safety, love, and adult leadership. Don’t smuggle in obedience.
new: Caution: The powerful technique of presupposition (embedding a statement as if it were true) is best used in the positive key of assuming choice, when it will occur, ability, not doing something unsafe, love, being adult, etc. Never use presupposition to imply that the other person must obey.

old: “Before any part has to change, it can first become more understood.”
new: “It is always the case that one can better understand something prior to changing it.”

old: A manipulative double bind traps every answer inside the speaker’s agenda. An ethical one offers two genuinely safe routes.
“Would this part prefer warmth first, or space first?”
new: Manipulative double bind questions:
Ethical double bind questions:
“What would be the best approach to this part, to warm it up or give it space?”

old: These are questions whose ordinary conversational form also acts as an invitation.
“Can the system show me the next step without showing me the whole wound?”
new: Example of a postulate in the form of a question:
“Isn’t it possible that the system can find a way to show me what it wants to show without showing me everything?”

old: Tag questions—isn’t it, can’t it, doesn’t it—can soften a sentence. They become oily very quickly, don’t they? Use them lightly.
new: Tag questions are sentences like "isn't it", "can't it", "doesn't it" at the end of a sentence. They can be a great way to soften up a sentence. They also get oily very fast, so use lightly.

old: “The body already knows something about resting, doesn’t it?”
new: Doesn't it already know how to do this?

old: Nominalizations turn processes into nouns: healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest. Their vagueness can sometimes help because the subconscious supplies its own concrete meaning.
new: Nominalizations are words like "healing", "safety", "trust", "integration", "communion", "clarity", "rest" etc. The beauty of these words is that, while they are vague to the conscious mind, they can be very specific to the subconscious. Try them out.

old: “A little more safety can arrive in whatever way the body understands.”
new: Can it allow itself more safety, in its own way?

old: More info, and a free intro session on my Somatic Guide. With SE, we track gently. Don’t turn the exercise into trauma excavation.
“Where is the activation?” “Where is the neutral place?” “Can attention move slowly between them?”
new: Would it be helpful for to know more or even experience a free intro session to how I work as a Somatic Guide?
It's not about thrusting into the trauma, in SE we learn to track.
The work might begin by tracking and discovering "Where is that activation", and "Where is a neutral place", and then "Where can we move, at a snail's pace, from one to the other?"

old: You were born with a mind that can dream, protect, analyze, imitate, love, remember, hide, reveal, and heal. Nobody taught its different layers how to speak to each other.
new: Have you ever considered the fact that you were born with an exquisitely designed and arranged brain and mind that is capable of many different layers of consciousness: dreaming, protecting, analyzing, imitating, loving, remembering, hiding, revealing and healing, etc. etc.?

old: Instead, most of us learned to push through, suppress emotion, perform confidence, obey or rebel against authority, and call that adulthood. Meanwhile, the deeper mind kept running its own programs: the child wanting safety, the guard expecting danger, the body remembering what the intellect had explained away, the intuition speaking before language, and the fantasy trying to become guidance.
new: Instead of learning how to integrate all of these different layers, you were taught (and/or you learned on your own) how to push, repress or supress your emotions, to pretend to be confident, to follow or defy authority, and so on and so forth. It is no wonder that you have many different "programs" running in your mind, including child mind, guard, body mind, intuitive mind, fantasy mind, etc.

old: A lot of hypnosis teaching treats the subconscious like a machine waiting for commands. That never did much for me. I get more from sitting down and listening until the scared kid, the guard, the body, the intuition, and the part trying to run Tuesday can all be heard without one of them seizing the microphone.
new: I learned hypnosis from a lot of people who tried to act as if the subconscious mind worked like a machine, and all they had to do was feed in a command and the machine would do what they put in. For me, a much more useful model was to learn to talk to different parts of myself until they all could listen together.

old: In this guide, self-hypnosis gathers attention until the conscious mind, subconscious, body, inner child, protectors, adult self, and Higher Self can participate in one honest inner meeting.
new: This guide teaches a method of self-hypnosis to bring the audience of the conscious mind, subconscious mind, body, inner child, protector parts, the adult self, and the Higher Self all into the same room to be able to listen and talk together.

old: The method is simple: listen, warm, protect, clarify, reality-test, and act.
new: Where do I start? Easy. Just listen, warm up to, protect, clarify, reality test and act on it!

old: A dramatic trance is optional. The goal is a more trustworthy relationship with the whole mind, proven in ordinary life.
new: It doesn’t have to be a dramatic trance experience but it does have to lead to a more trustworthy relationship between all parts of the mind.

old: Communion is the closest word I have for that. The conscious mind stops shouting from the roof, and the subconscious no longer has to communicate only through symptoms, dreams, cravings, daydreams, and peculiar little body signals.
new: Let’s call it communion. The conscious mind doesn’t have to shout it’s message from the roof top and the subconscious doesn’t have to rely on symptoms, dreams, cravings, day dreams, and other weird body signals to communicate.

old: I treat the subconscious as a living ecology of parts, memories, impulses, images, protections, and wisdom. I bring in inner-child reparenting because a wounded young part won’t be repaired by a clever suggestion. I begin with Higher Self or the universal heart when the system needs coherence, and separate into parts only when that helps. I borrow from prompt engineering because the shape of a question changes the kind of answer we can hear. And I include influence literacy because hypnosis is hardly the only thing hypnotizing us.
new: I work with the premise that the subconscious is an ecology, and we must be skilled enough to communicate with its many parts, to separate ourselves into those parts if necessary to better understand them, to heal inner child trauma by reparenting those parts, to coalesce that ecology into a Higher Self or universal heart when need be, and more. I also pull in elements from prompt engineering, and teach literacy in the domain of influence, since hypnosis is far from the only thing that’s hypnotizing us.

old: The subconscious isn’t the enemy. Neither are the body, the sharp analytical mind, or the protector that has been braced for years. Most of them have been trying to help without ever being properly introduced.
new: Hi, I’m Sarah. I believe that your subconscious mind, your body, your analytical mind, and the part of you that feels like it needs to protect you are all on your side.

old: I’m less interested in how deeply you can get hypnotized than whether you become an adult you can trust.
new: Whether or not you can “get hypnotized” isn’t as important to me as whether or not you can become a trustworthy adult.

old: Personal relaxation-tech note: On my ZHoly3O page, I discuss ozonated charcoal “holy water” as one relaxation support, and I also mention Blushield. These remain optional supports. They don’t prove that any inner signal is true. Stabilize the body, listen gently, reality-test, and return to one grounded action.
new: See my ZHoly3O page for more on the use of ozonated charcoal, “holy water” as an important tool in the protocol of relaxing. Use of Blushield is also detailed there, and may be of some benefit, although not at all essential. The important thing is to get the body to a state of stabilization where one can begin to discern between valid and non-valid messages from the “inner realm”. Once reality tested, take appropriate actions to restore oneself to a grounded state.

old: First, body. Feet, chair, breath, room.
new: Where is my body? What are my feet doing? What is my butt doing? How am I sitting in the chair? How am I breathing? What is my body doing in this room?

old: Little one, I am here. Protector, thank you for warning me. You do not have to scream for me to listen.
new: And if you can hear me, little one, know that I am here and that I am here to protect you. Thank you, protector, for alerting me. You do not need to scream. I got the message.

old: If there is real action needed, show me one step. If there is no action needed, help the body stand down gently.
new: Now if there is something my body needs to do, show me what the first step is for my body to do right now. And if there is nothing my body can do right now, help my body stand down.

old: I will not abandon the signal. I will not worship the signal. I will listen, test, and act.
new: I won’t abandon you, but I won’t worship you either.

old: Use this checklist when a person, advertisement, ideology, spiritual teaching, romantic pull, or inner voice is pressing too hard.

“I notice influence is happening. I do not need to obey it or attack it. I can slow down. I can ask what is being presupposed. I can ask who benefits. I can notice what my body is signaling without assuming what it proves. I can ask what love, truth, humility, and ordinary life would require.
new: Use this checklist when any person, ad, ideology, spiritual teaching, romantic attraction, or voice inside of yourself tries to exert influence over…

old: If this is true, it will survive questions. If this is love, it will survive boundaries. If this is guidance, it will survive sleep. If this is for me, it will not require me to abandon my adult self.”
Before acting, ask:
Is there urgency?
Is there secrecy?
Is there shame?
Is there a threat of exclusion?
Is there a promise of specialness?
Is there sexual charge?
new: Ask yourself: If this is really true, will it still be there when I’m questioning it? If this is really love, will it still be there when I put healthy boundaries? If this is really guidance, will it still be there when I’ve slept on it? If this is really meant for me, will it still be there when I accept that I’m an adult now?
Before acting, also ask yourself: Is there a sense of urgency here? A sense of secrecy? A sense of shame? A threat of being left out? A promise of specialness? A sexual charge?

old: Is there spiritual superiority?
new: Are some people being put forward as spiritually superior?

old: Is there a demand for money, sex, loyalty, silence, or obedience?
new: Is there a demand that something be given up – money, sex, loyalty, silence, obedience?

old: Is there a narrowing of choices?
new: Is there a narrowing of choices for yourself?

old: Is questioning treated as betrayal?
new: Is any questioning considered a betrayal?

old: Is resistance pathologized?
new: Is there a way of making resistance seem pathological?

old: Is ordinary life being downgraded?
new: Is there a down-grading of ordinary life?

old: Is the child part being seduced, scared, or rescued?
new: Is there a seduction, or scaring or rescuing of the child in?

old: Is the adult self still allowed to say no?
new: Can the adult in still say “no” ?

old: Several yes answers mean slow down. Don’t deepen trance or make an irreversible decision. Return to the room, body, food, sleep, time, and counsel.
new: If you found yourself saying yes to any of these, several in fact, then maybe it’s time to stop going deeper, and to make irreversible decisions until you can get back into the room, in your body, connected to food, sleep, time, and good counsel.

old: A good guide increases your adult self. A bad guide replaces it. A good guide can tolerate your no. A bad guide calls your no resistance, ego, fear, low vibration, trauma, sin, or proof that you need more of their guidance.
new: And by the way, a good guide increases your adult self; a bad one replaces it. A good guide can tolerate your “no”; a bad one will reframe it as resistance or ego or fear or low vibration or past trauma or sin, or just more evidence of the need for more guidance.

old: Before accepting a recording or live suggestion, ask:
Was I plainly told that induction mechanics are being used?
Can at least one answer lead to pause, modification, full alertness, or stopping?
Does the speaker treat not noticing as secret proof that the process worked?
Are roles, ownership, obedience, age, identity, or belonging being used to lower adult judgment?
new: Did somebody not tell, plainly, that induction mechanics would be used?
Is at least one answer likely to get someone pausing, modding, full on, or stoping?
Does it imply that not noticing it was a secret proof that it worked?
Did it use roles, ownership, obedience, age, identity, or belong-ness, to get an adult to not use their judgement?

old: Are fractionation, cues, later behavior, or memory effects disclosed before they are used?
new: Do they tell first, rather than sneak in fractionation, cues, later behavior or memory effects?

old: Are ordinary body sensations being turned into evidence for a hidden claim?
new: Are they exploiting body sensations?

old: Does the exit restore ordinary identity, movement, orientation, and critical judgment—and plainly say that the session has ended?
new: Do they carefully restore all aspects of identity, movement, orientation and critical ability and tell explicitly the session is over when coming out?

old: When an answer is unclear, stay fully alert. Ask for the exact script, change the method, or leave.
new: If in doubt on any of these, come fully out of it, ask to see a copy of the script, change to a different method, or stop altogether.
